recentItems.title: Mother who lost three sons in Srebrenica massacre reacts to death of Mladic
recentItems.description:
(28 Aug 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Srebrenica, Bosnia - 28 August 2026
1. Various aerials of Srebrenica memorial site ++ MUTE++
2. Various aerials of praying by grave ++MUTE++
3. Aerial of graves  ++MUTE++
4. Mid of tombstone 
5. Mid of graves 
6. Close of memorial stone 
7. Various of people by memorial 
8. Various of graves 
9. Mejra Djogaz sitting at the table
10. SOUNDBITE (Bosnian) Mejra Djogaz, mother of victims of 1995 Srebrenica massacre:
"They killed my eldest son born in 1972, Zudi, Munib born in 1974 and Omar born in 1976.” 
11. Close of Mejra's hand
12. SOUNDBITE (Bosnian) Mejra Djogaz, mother of victims of 1995 Srebrenica massacre:
"I wish he lived longer to suffer and to be in pain, but he left this world.” 
13. Various of graves
STORYLINE:
A mother who lost family members during the 1995 Srebrenica massacre reacted on Thursday to the death of former Bosnian Serb general Ratko Mladic whose forces carried out the worst massacre in Europe since World War II.

Mladic died Thursday while serving a life sentence for his crimes, U.N. officials said. He was 84.

The U.N. tribunal for war crimes committed during the wars in the former Yugoslavia in the 1990s sentenced Mladic to life in prison in 2017 in what was considered a key step toward bringing justice to the victims.

He had been in custody since 2011 after many years on the run.

"I wish he lived longer to suffer and to be in pain, but he left this world," said Mejra Djogaz, the mother of several victims of the 1995 massacre.

The ruthless, blue-eyed former communist officer-turned nationalist warlord was one of the most notorious figures of the conflict that left more than 100,000 people dead and over 1 million homeless.

He commanded his troops to “scorch the brains” of the Bosnian Muslims and boasted of being a “Serbian God.”

When the ethnic war in Bosnia and Herzegovina started in 1992, Mladic became the commander of the Bosnian Serb troops and took control of large swaths of the country to form a Serb mini-state.

Serbs under Mladic’s control laid siege to the Bosnian capital, Sarajevo, and other cities and villages, established concentration camps for detained non-Serb civilians and enemy soldiers, and systematically killed prisoners.

In Sarajevo, Serb troops kept the city isolated while killing civilians with snipers and heavy artillery.

In 1995, Mladic’s troops slaughtered more than 8,000 Muslim men and boys in Srebrenica — the first case of genocide in Europe since WWII.

But Mladic and his admirers have never repented.

He was seen by many as a patriot fighting for the first pan-Serbian state.

Defiant, Mladic acted bullishly during his trial and yelled at the judges when sentenced to life in prison.

AP video shot by: Almir Alic

recentItems.title: China MOFA briefing highlights
recentItems.description:
(28 Aug 2026) 
ASSOCIATED PRESS
Beijing, China - 28 August 2026

Spokesperson: Lin Jian 

1.Today, the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee held a meeting to discuss and make arrangements for emergency rescue efforts following the mudslide disaster in Gyirong county, Shigatse City, Tibet. Can you provide any information on this matter?

The meeting emphasized that this disaster occurred in a high-altitude, frigid region, where valleys are steep and weather is unpredictable. There are still numerous glaciers, glacial lakes, and potential geological hazards in the surrounding area, causing enormous difficulties for rescue operations. All relevant parties must uphold the principle of putting people and human lives first and ensure all work is carried out with resolute and effective measures and scientifically sound and efficient methods. Search and rescue plans must be scientifically formulated, and every effort must be made to locate missing persons from both China and abroad. Joint consultations among multiple departments should be strengthened, along with monitoring and early-warning efforts. Close attention should be paid to the stability of the barrier lake and surrounding mountains, and effective measures should be taken to prevent secondary disasters. The management of personnel on-site must be strengthened to ensure safety throughout the entire rescue process. Proper arrangements must be made for the affected population and all follow-up work, such as compensation and relief efforts, must be carried out in a thorough and meticulous manner. Emergency assistance should be provided to the disaster-hit areas in Nepal and international rescue cooperation should be carried out. 
We will earnestly implement the spirit of the meeting of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and spare no effort in carrying out emergency response, rescue operations and other foreign-related work. 

2.Does China have any official determination on the cause of the deadly mudslide?

We noted that experts and official institutions from both China and Nepal have already made some assessments regarding the causes of this disaster. According to their analysis, the disaster may have been triggered by a high-altitude glacier collapse in Nepal. For more details, please refer to the information released by the relevant Chinese authorities.

3.We noted the reports earlier this morning that 555 tourists have all been evacuated. There are reportedly many Indian tourists among them. Could you confirm whether all Indian tourists have been evacuated, or if there are any stranded? 

As I mentioned earlier, the relevant information is still being verified. We have already notified the embassies of the countries concerned in China and will continue to maintain communication with them.

4.It is reported that the results of the Cook Islands parliamentary election showed that the Cook Islands Party, led by incumbent Prime Minister Mark Brown, won a majority of seats, and Brown is set to serve another term as prime minister. What is China's comment and what are China’s expectations for China-Cook Islands relations?


5.US President Donald Trump yesterday hinted that his government was preparing to sanction Chinese banks linked to Iran. What is the Chinese side’s comment?

Regarding the situation in Iran, we believe that dialogue and negotiations are the only way out of the current situation. China’s opposition to illegal unilateral sanctions is consistent and clear.
STORYLINE:


===========================================================

recentItems.title: People gather to watch the lunar eclipse in the city of Marica, Brazil
recentItems.description:
(28 Aug 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Maricá, Brazil - 28 August 2026
++NIGHT SHOTS++
1. Various of lunar eclipse 
2. Mid of people gathering at Maricá planetarium 
3. Mid of people at Maricá Planetarium observing lunar eclipse 
4. Mid of woman observing lunar eclipse through telescope 
5. Mid of people using binoculars to observe lunar eclipse 
6. Wide of Man observing lunar eclipse with binoculars
7. Mid of person watching live feed of lunar eclipse on phone
8. Mid of visitors observing lunar eclipse through telescope 
9. SOUNDBITE (Portuguese) Jackson de Farias, director of the Maricá Planetarium:
"It is certainly an event that, since it doesn't happen all the time, generates interest and captures people's attention. And when they come here, we try to increasingly pique their curiosity and make them leave with more questions than answers. That's the little key we turn to make people come back here and spark the curiosity that everyone has. It's not just children who are curious, right? It's an attempt we have to popularize science and astronomy as a whole."
10. Close of lunar eclipse 
STORYLINE:
Residents in Maricá looked to the skies as Brazil experienced a lunar eclipse overnight. 

People gathered at the planetarium in Maricá, a coastal city in Rio de Janeiro state, to watch the eclipse as the moon passed through Earth’s shadow.

The celestial event could be seen with the naked eye, while telescopes were made available to the public for a closer look at the moon as it changed in appearance.

Beginning in the Americas, nearly the entire lunar surface was masked Thursday night into Friday, with up to 96% of the moon covered, making it an especially deep partial eclipse.

The event came two weeks after a total solar eclipse crossed Greenland, Iceland and Spain.

Eclipses always travel in pairs as the sun, moon and Earth align so precisely that one obscures the other.

That’s because the moon is 400 times smaller than the sun, which is 400 times farther away, making them appear the same size - a cosmic coincidence and gift from the universe.

The lunar eclipse was visible across parts of North and South America, Europe, Africa and the Middle East.

recentItems.title: Relatives traumatised after family members killed in Nepal floods
recentItems.description:
(28 Aug 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Nuwakot, Nepal - 28 August 2026
1. Official announcing flood warning using megaphone UPSOUND No name given (Nepali): "A flood is coming from Rasuwagadhi, do not go forward, move backwards, stay away from the river."
2. Tracking shot of closed shops
3. Pan from closed shops to road, people walking on road
4. Wide of road
5. Wide of helicopter flying above
6. Various of bereaved woman Shristi Maya Tamang crying
7. SOUNDBITE (Hindi) Dawa Lama, family member of flood victims:
"I have returned from South Korea. I have been working there for three years for livelihood."
8. Mid of bereaved sitting on ground
9. SOUNDBITE (Hindi) Dawa Lama, family member of flood victims:
"My village, my lineage, my family, all are dead. My father, sister, my relatives are no more. Today, I met my father in law, it was good to meet him."
10. Wide of people sitting on ground
11. SOUNDBITE (Nepali) Ghyamba Tsering, local resident:
"My wife and son were taken by the flood. My whole village was taken by the flood. Almost all the roads were also swept away by the flood. All the bridges were also gone. A few of the roads were still there so I walked along those roads and reached here."
12. Tracking shot of residents 
STORYLINE:
In Nuwakot, Nepal, families members who lost loved ones in a devastating flash flood grieved on Friday, as authorities warned residents to stay away from swollen rivers.

Rescuers worked through mud and debris in areas devastated by a catastrophic flash flood along the Himalayan border between Nepal and China, continuing the search for hundreds of people still missing as the death toll rose and authorities warned that a newly formed, overflowing lake could trigger further flooding.

Bereaved relatives described losing multiple family members and entire communities to the floodwaters, which also swept away roads and bridges.

"My village, my lineage, my family, all are dead. My father, sister, my relatives are no more," said Dawa Lama, who returned from South Korea. 

Nepal police said Friday morning that the country’s death toll had risen to 469 from 390 a day earlier, as rescuers recover more bodies amid the debris. 

China has not updated its report of just three deaths in Tibet. Together, the two countries have said that more than 1,500 people are missing.

AP video shot by: Rishi Lekhi

"His death, well he died of natural causes, from old age, this would come anyway, its God's will. But us, the victims, are satisfied, when we know that he was convicted to life in jail. For us, its important that he is convicted and that he served his sentence until he was dead."

"So what is worrying here is that even after his death, the political narrative of glorification, celebration, calling him 'general hero' will increase and intensify from Bosnian Serb parties, but also from Serbian parties in Serbia. That is the problem that will remain with us."

recentItems.title: Stargazers, families and astronomers camp outside Caracas planetarium to see partial lunar eclipse
recentItems.description:
(28 Aug 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

++NIGHT SHOTS++
ASSOCIATED PRESS
Caracas - 28 August 2026
1. Various of children watching the moon covered by clouds. UPSOUND (Spanish) “Oh no, it’s hiding!”
2. Timelapse of moon behind clouds
3. Person looking at eclipse through telescope
4. Partial eclipse
5. Hector Garcia and his family watching the eclipse
6. Various of Garcia and his son taking pictures of the moon with telescope
7. SOUNDBITE (Spanish) Hector Garcia, veterinarian:

“In 15 minutes it will be my birthday, and I have this eclipse as a birthday present”
8. Wide of people camping,  watching eclipse
9. People taking pictures of eclipse
10. People watching eclipse
STORYLINE:
Stargazers, families and astronomers camped outside planetarium in Caracas to see the partial lunar eclipse.

A dense cloudy sky during the beginning of the night made people anxious, fearing they could not see  it.

But just as the shadow began to grow on the moon, the clouds slowly disappeared. the sky cleared and people could see the entirety of the eclipse. 

"It's turning red!", kids shouted

Hector Garcia and his family set a tent and a telescope to watch the eclipse together. 

Garcia, a veterinarian, began his obsession with the universe and the sky when he gifted his son a telescope. 

Together they have learned about the planets and watch cosmic events together whenever they can. 

The night of the eclipse also happened to be Garcia's birthday.

I was even worried when they transferred me to Sokoto, thinking of what I was going to do in Sokoto. But when I entered Sokoto, I see, the life is easy. I always go out, even on Friday, Saturday, Sunday, just to go and have some fun with my friends and maybe once in a while with my family.”
10. Various of night revellers in a nightclub
11. SOUNDBITE (English) Usman Abdullahi Jatau, Sokoto Hisbah Commander:
“Hisbah was established to enjoin good and abstain from evil. Not only to deliberate the Islamic Sharia directly, as some people are looking at Hisbah. We attend to every citizen in Nigeria, be him or her a Muslim or non-Muslim, and we do justice to every one of us. Ours is to see how we can uphold, how we can promote good morals and virtues within and outside the state.”
12. Various of night revellers in a nightclub
13. SOUNDBITE (English) Oluwamayowa Idowu, Founder, Culture Custodian:
“A large part of nightlife is escapism. So, you want to have an experience that takes you away from your day-to-day. And so, yes, the North has kind of been ravaged by insecurity and insurgency, but people still live there. People still participate in life there on a daily basis. So again, it's not surprising that they are looking at nightlife as one of the ways through which they can escape and express themselves.”
14. Various of night revellers
15. SOUNDBITE (English) Oluwamayowa Idowu, Founder, Culture Custodian:
“If we take out insecurity from northern Nigeria, I think the nightlife culture would be bigger than what it is. But I do think it will still be limited by the religious undertone that is common in the north.” 
16. Various of nightlife revellers
STORYLINE:
The dance floor was still half empty after 11pm on a Friday night in July in Sokoto, Nigeria. There were few signs the evening would turn into a boisterous party of sweaty bodies and shrill voices singing along to the sound of Afrobeats.

Multicoloured strobes flashed across the walls and tables as the DJ assembled his set. Club attendants arranged bottles of expensive alcohol on the tables in different sections. 

It was an unlikely club scene in Sokoto, a deeply conservative ancient Nigerian state called the “seat of the caliphate” for its storied place in the birth and propagation of Islam in West and Central Africa.

The nightclub is one of the handful in town in the region where a bustling night scene runs an uneasy cohabitation with deep conservative religious codes across northern Nigeria, where Boko Haram has waged a seventeen-year-long Islamist insurgency and, more recently, the Islamic State.
